items.q: Which classic midbrain sign on T2-weighted brain MRI is characteristic of neurological Wilson's disease?
items.exp: The midbrain MRI photo and caption highlight the 'Face of giant panda' sign. (Book p1017)

items.q: Match each brain MRI finding in Wilson's disease with its neuroanatomical location — 1) Mercedes-Benz sign 2) Bright Claustrum sign … A) Hyperintensity in the thin gray matter claustrum lateral to the putamen B) Trisected hyperintensity in the pons
items.exp: The Mercedes-Benz sign corresponds to 'Trisected pontine' hyperintensity; the Bright Claustrum sign shows bilateral claustrum hyperintensity. (Book p1017)

items.q: Which of the following MRI abnormalities is NOT illustrated on this page for Wilson's disease?
items.exp: Illustrated MRI signs are Basal ganglia hyperintensity, Face of giant panda, Thalamic hyperintensity, Bisected pontine hyperintensity, Mercedes Benz sign (trisected pontine), and Bright Claustrum sign. (Book p1017)

items.q: What is the mode of inheritance and responsible gene in classic adult hereditary hemochromatosis?
opts: Autosomal recessive, defect in the HFE gene on chromosome 6p
Autosomal dominant, defect in the ATP7B gene on chromosome 13q
X-linked recessive, defect in the ferroportin gene
Autosomal recessive, defect in the hemojuvelin gene on chromosome 1q
items.exp: Hereditary hemochromatosis is autosomal recessive, caused by a defect in the HFE gene on chromosome 6p. (Book p1017)

items.q: At what stage of life does classic adult hereditary hemochromatosis typically become clinically manifest?
items.exp: The book notes: 'Adult : 4th to 5th decade' for HFE-related hemochromatosis. (Book p1017)

items.q: Match each genotype of the C282Y HFE mutation with its clinical association — 1) Homozygous C282Y 2) Heterozygous C282Y … A) Porphyria cutanea tarda (PCT) and NASH B) Full-blown hereditary hemochromatosis
items.exp: Homozygous C282Y causes hemochromatosis, whereas heterozygous C282Y is associated with PCT (Porphyria cutanea tarda) and NASH. (Book p1017)

items.q: Which non-HFE genes are responsible for early-onset Juvenile Hemochromatosis?
items.exp: Non-HFE juvenile hemochromatosis involves 'Hemojuvelin transferrin receptor-2' and 'Hepcidin'. (Book p1017)

items.q: Assess the two statements: I Co-existing alcohol consumption markedly accelerates the progression to cirrhosis in patients with hereditary hemochromatosis. II The Bright Claustrum sign on MRI is pathognomonic for Wilson's disease.
items.exp: Both statements are true: alcohol increases cirrhosis risk in hemochromatosis, and the Bright Claustrum sign is demonstrated in Wilson's disease. (Book p1017)
